# Ateles: chronic tax vs acute crisis (frame-product-argument)

## Subject

What the solo technical founder-operator ICP tolerates daily versus what converts them to adopt Ateles.

## Summary

Acute leads: an untraceable, unattributed high-blast agent action already taken (a merge, a payment, a message) converts harder than the chronic tax of manual multi-chat coordination and context loss, because the chronic tax is a cost the operator has already decided to absorb.

## Body

Chronic: The operator coordinates multiple agent chats by hand, opening a new one per task and hoping concurrent ones do not conflict. Nothing persists between sessions, so context is re-explained every time — project state, prior decisions, constraints. Coordination logic accretes as a growing CLAUDE.md and scattered shell scripts rather than any declared workflow. This is diffuse, cumulative, and survivable: an operator absorbs it for months because each single instance costs only a few extra minutes of re-explaining or a bit of copy-paste glue, and nothing about it looks urgent on any given day (docs/foundation/charter.md, origin/main: 'coordination is ad-hoc, starting a multi-agent workflow means opening chats by hand and hoping they do not conflict, and the operator pays the difference in bespoke scripts and manual sync').

Acute: The concrete failure is discovering, after the fact, that an agent took a consequential action — a merge, a payment, an outbound message — with no reconstructable record of who authorized it or under what scope, because the agent acted under the operator's own shared identity with no distinct attribution. The cost is discoverable and specific: an action the operator cannot explain, defend, or undo cleanly, surfacing exactly when it matters (a bad merge that shipped, a payment that should have been checkpointed, an email sent that should not have gone out). Per README.md (origin/main): 'identities collapse — a code-writing agent acts as you on GitHub, with no audit trail tying the signed subject to the action' and 'decisions execute without a reproducible trail — you can't trace why an agent did something or whether it [stayed in scope]'.

Leads: ACUTE LEADS. The chronic tax (manual sequencing, context loss) is the more relatable and easier pain to write copy about, but per the register's own standing rule (plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f, decision 'problem_leads_the_hero': the hero states the problem, and per the frame-product-argument skill's chronic/acute doctrine) a reader who recognizes a tax they have already decided to absorb has no reason to act today. The acute crisis — an untraceable, unattributed high-blast action already taken — is the strongest single qualifier: it is the moment the operator can name the problem precisely and go looking for a fix, and it is also the failure mode the competitor test (research_finding ent_f8271efcdb842076a5147929) found NOT claimable by a generic orchestration framework, which has no concept of authority or accountability. The existing settled headline candidate for this lead, from the same decision register, is 'Agents are cheap. Organizations are not.' (parent problem statement, plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f overview) — this pain analysis supplies the chronic/acute mechanics under that headline; it does not propose a different headline.

Reviewed by: pm.

## Gaps

No field-verified customer research (icp_signal / customer_development_note) exists for Ateles on this Neotoma instance to corroborate which pain actually converts a real prospect — both the chronic and acute descriptions and the lead call are derived from the product's own stated rationale for existing (charter.md, README.md), not from interviews or outreach signal. This should be treated as a reasoned hypothesis to validate against real conversations, not a confirmed finding.
